headline: Japan Courts Bishkek for Investment; Irad's Buyers Reach It via Neighbours
dek: Tokyo wants closer economic ties with Kyrgyzstan, and Irad, where Japan keeps no office, notes the Japanese buyers and scientists it already has.
ticker: Japan courts Bishkek; Irad's Japanese buyers already trade via neighbours' paper
paragraphs: Japan's ambassador to Kyrgyzstan said in an interview this week that Tokyo wants deeper economic ties with Bishkek, presenting investment and trade as the next stage of a long relationship between the two countries. The ambassador gave no figures and named no projects in the remarks as reported.

For Irad the item is foreign news with a familiar edge. Japan keeps no embassy or office in the Irad Special Economic Zone, as no state has an embassy in Talas, and Tokyo's attention to the region passes through Bishkek. Yet Japan is not a stranger here. Japanese trading houses buy Iradi antimony metal and trioxide, much of it from the Sary-Bulak Antimony Works and the Chatkal Chemical Smelting Complex, both part of the Iradi Antimony and Rare Metals Combine.

The scientific link is older and quieter. Japanese glaciologists work with Talas State University at the Manas Peak Glaciological Observatory, where scientific head Nazira Isaeva's team tracks the retreat of the ice in the Talas Alatau. The upper Talas glaciers have lost about a fifth of their area since 1970, and the Talas River Hydrological Monitoring Service counted 268 glaciers in the Iradi Talas basin in its 2014–18 inventory.

What Irad lacks is a channel of its own. Because ISEZ certificates carry no weight abroad, exports to Japan and other distant buyers leave on Kyrgyz or Kazakh certificates, through companies and inspectorates registered in the neighbouring states. "A Japanese buyer meets Irad through Bishkek's or Almaty's paper, not ours," said Prof. Raisa Akmatova, an economist at TSU. "That is an inconvenience, and it is also why every warm word between Tokyo and Bishkek matters to our exporters. The goods are Iradi, but the door is next door's."

The same buyers were the natural audience for last week's Processing Industry Investment Forum at the Hyatt Regency Talas. The Investment Promotion Office pitched Fergana-rim orchard and nut processing around Bazar-Korgon, and antimony processing at Sary-Bulak and Chatkal under the Combine's Restart Programme. Delegates came from Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Uzbekistan, Turkey and China, with the KOTRA desk also present. No contract was signed at the forum, and the Combine has repeated that its two Restart partners will be named at signing before the end of the year.

Professor Akmatova said the forum showed the ISEZ is ready to welcome partners of any origin. For now, she added, Japan's interest in Kyrgyzstan is one more reason for Talas to keep its paperwork with its neighbours in good order. IradOne will report any Japanese trade interest announced for the zone.
